summary: Tenant-initiated pin-refresh race overwrote explicit model selection mid-stream
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that during a rolling canary in us-east, long-lived streaming sessions for specific tenants suddenly switched from the tenant-requested model (explicit model_version header) to a canary variant. The switch happened without any client-side reconnect and while the stream was mid-response. This appears correlated with a background pin-refresh operation initiated by the tenant SDK at the same time the control-plane applied a reconciliation update.

Impact:
- Several production customers experienced inconsistent outputs for in-flight streams (approx 30 affected sessions over a 20m window).
- Outputs from the canary variant produced tokenization/format deltas, causing 3 downstream user-facing failures (alerts from customer evals).
- Customer Covalent Analytics (dedicated tier) reports degraded ML QA scores and asked for urgent mitigation.

Environment:
- prod, us-east primary (edge), eu-west had a smaller blast radius via cross-region routing fallback
- Affected tenant on Dedicated capacity pool (reserved), interacting with a staged canary weight shift for redwood/v1-chat-13b -> redwood/quant-4bit-7b variant

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Start a long-lived streaming session (server-side streaming) with header: "model_version: redwood/v1-chat-13b@2024-10-31" and tenant pin metadata in X-Redwood-Tenant-Pin
2) Trigger a tenant token refresh (SDK auto refresh) from client, which calls control-plane pin-refresh endpoint for lease renewal (~client-side refresh every 15m; here it occurred mid-stream)
3) Simultaneously the orchestrator applied a canary snapshot update and a reconciliation loop merged a prewarm snapshot into the control-plane routing table
4) During the next prefix/KV reconciliation window, edge dropped model_version affinity and routed mid-stream traffic to the canary lane

Observed behavior:
- Edge logs show a Control-Plane:PATCH routing update at 2024-11-05T17:03:12Z followed by an edge decision to remap requests from model_id redwood/v1-chat-13b to redwood/quant-4bit-7b at 17:03:14Z for the affected session ids.
- The HTTP/2 stream remained open (no reconnect from customer) and server continued generating; model switch appears to have been applied in-path by sidecar routing decisions.

Relevant logs (snippets):
- edge-proxy (us-east-1) 2024-11-05T17:03:12.217Z INFO "received controlplane routing patch" request_id=xyz-331
- front-proxy decision 2024-11-05T17:03:14.009Z WARN "session-routing: replacing pinned variant for session" session_id=abc-902 tenant_id=cov-17 old_variant=redwood/v1-chat-13b new_variant=redwood/quant-4bit-7b reason=controlplane-merge
- sidecar sanitizer 2024-11-05T17:03:14.011Z DEBUG "header mutate: tenant pin refresh token detected, applying ttl extension"
- serving-runtime 2024-11-05T17:03:14.120Z INFO "accepted request on model redwood/quant-4bit-7b" request_id=req-771

Notes on reproduction attempts:
- With a synthetic streaming workload (10 parallel long-lived streams) we could reproduce the mid-stream switch ~60% of runs when timing the SDK refresh to coincide with a control-plane canary apply.
- Reproduces more reliably when prefix/KV cache warmup is in-progress (suggests race between cache application and pin affinity checks).
comments: 2024-11-05 18:02 - Samira Kapoor (Support): Acknowledged. Reproduced locally with synthetic harness. Captured full traces and saved link to slack: #support-thread SUP-770070. Initial hypothesis: reconciliation ordering + sidecar TTL extension race.

2024-11-05 19:15 - Diego Morales (SRE): Correlated with PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1842 — that change introduced prewarm snapshot merges during canary apply. Adding Diego as assignee to investigate ordering guarantees.

2024-11-05 20:03 - Covalent Analytics (customer): We saw three user sessions produce hallucinated product IDs after the switch. Client would prefer a strong guarantee that explicit model headers are immutable for session lifetime.

2024-11-06 09:30 - Riley Chen (Runtime): Observed that serving-runtime accepts requests based on sidecar routing metadata. Sidecar was performing header mutation for TTL extension which reset affinity check to control-plane computed value. Adding runtime guard to prefer explicit header if present.

2024-11-07 11:10 - Diego Morales (SRE): Mitigation deployed to us-east: control-plane changed merge ordering to apply 'session-affinity-preserve' flag earlier; sidecar patch rolled to avoid TTL extension mutating affinity identifier mid-stream. Monitoring for 24h.

2024-11-07 12:04 - Covalent Analytics (customer): Confirmed no further mid-stream switches in the monitored window. Thank you — requesting postmortem and a config to enforce strict-model pins for their tenant going forward.

2024-11-07 15:20 - Samira Kapoor (Support): Added follow-up items: (1) create alert for \"midstream-model-variant-switch\" > 1/min, (2) add unit tests in control-plane for merge ordering, (3) document tenant opt-in flag for strict pin preservation in Confluence runbook.
investigation_notes: Investigative timeline: 11/05 reproduce -> captured edge+sidecar+control-plane traces; 11/06 isolated race between control-plane snapshot merge and sidecar TTL mutation; 11/06 runtime team proposed short-term guard to prefer explicit model_version header; 11/07 mitigation deployed to us-east. Hypothesis: sidecar TTL extension logic inadvertently replaced session-affinity token used by edge for routing during reconciliation. Other contributing factor: prefix/KV warmup during canary prewarm causes transient path where control-plane computed routing is temporarily preferred.
resolution: Hotfix deployed (control-plane PR #1842 reverted the merge ordering change and added an explicit 'preserve-explicit-model' flag during routing table apply; sidecar patch prevents TTL extension from overwriting affinity token mid-stream). Workaround offered to customer: (A) add explicit X-Redwood-Strict-Pin: true header to enforce immutable pin for session lifetime, (B) stagger SDK refresh windows or disable auto pin-refresh during critical streams. Customer accepted workaround and requested strict pin config (scheduled as follow-up).
follow_up_tasks: Create Confluence postmortem and link to this ticket
Add e2e test coverage for long-lived streams + pin-refresh during canary apply
Implement alerting for midstream model switches (>1/min threshold)
Add tenant-level config flag for strict pin preservation (product + security review needed)
